findings.issue_text: Team permission check in addGuests.handler.ts uses && instead of ||: isTeamAdminOrOwner requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner, wrongly denying team admins who are not owners and effectively breaking the team-admin authorization path

BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS blacklist is bypassable via case variation: guest input is never normalized and comparisons are exact-string, so Banned@Example.com bypasses a banned@example.com entry; also no .trim() on split blacklist entries, so entries with leading/trailing whitespace never match
Exact-string comparison (guest === attendee.email) lets case variants defeat the duplicate guest filter, allowing the same person to be added twice

Guest email uniqueness is only enforced client-side: the refine lives only in AddGuestsDialog.tsx while the server schema is just z.array(z.string().email()) and uniqueGuests only dedupes against existing attendees — a direct API call with duplicate emails creates duplicate attendee rows and sends duplicate emails/ICS invites

No upper bound on the guests array (no .max()) and no rate limiting on the mutation, so any authorized user (including a mere attendee) can submit thousands of emails in one request, each producing a DB row and a full-details scheduled email — an outbound spam/DoS vector

Calendar update uses the requester's credentials instead of the organizer's: getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) is passed to EventManager while the organizer's credentials (explicitly included in the booking query) are never used, so when a non-organizer adds guests, updateCalendarAttendees runs with the wrong or empty credential set and guests are never added to the organizer's actual calendar event (or the update errors out)

Raw guests array is passed to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of uniqueGuests, so an existing attendee whose email appears in the filtered-out list matches newGuests.includes(attendee.email) in email-manager.ts and receives a full AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the correct guests-added notification

No booking status or time check: the findFirst has no status filter, so guests can be added to CANCELLED/REJECTED or long-past bookings, generating CONFIRMED ICS invites and calendar updates for events that no longer exist and misleading recipients

Partial-state failure: eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees is not wrapped in error handling, so if it throws the mutation returns an error even though the guests were already added (no rollback), and a retry behaves unexpectedly
Email sending errors are swallowed: the catch block logs only a static string (Error sending AddGuestsEmails) and discards err, making delivery failures invisible

Stale validation error in AddGuestsDialog.tsx: setIsInvalidEmail(true) is never reset when the user retries with corrected input (only cleared via the Cancel button), so the error banner persists after the input becomes valid

The `guests` array in addGuests.schema.ts has no `.max()` cap, so a single authenticated request can submit thousands of emails, driving unbounded `createMany` rows, unbounded calendar API attendee pushes, and unbounded email fan-out — SMTP/provider quota exhaustion, sender-IP reputation damage (an email-bombing/spam vector through the mail infrastructure), DB bloat, and CPU burn
Every add-guests call re-emails all existing attendees rather than just the new guests, so repeated calls amplify email volume to roughly k×N emails

Each fanned-out email requires a full `generateIcsString` call that itself iterates all attendees (O(N²) work per call) plus a React SSR render, all dispatched concurrently via one unbounded `Promise.all`; one ICS payload could be shared per role

addGuests.handler.ts fetches the organizer's credentials via `include: { credentials: true }` (heavy OAuth token blobs) but never reads them, while `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` issues a second credentials query for the requester — a duplicate load when the requester is the organizer, and in the attendee-initiated path the EventManager is built from the wrong user's credentials, causing `updateCalendarAttendees` to no-op or error against the organizer's calendar references

N+1 translation loads: `getTranslation(attendee.locale)` is invoked per attendee inside a map, performing O(attendees) i18n resource loads/instantiations on every add-guests request; translations should be cached per distinct locale

Linear-scan membership checks inside loops: `booking.attendees.some(...)` per guest (addGuests.handler.ts:74–78) and `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` per attendee (email-manager.ts:~541) are both O(N×M); a `Set` should be used for lookups

Blanket cache invalidation: `utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate()` in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:37 invalidates every query under `viewer.bookings`, triggering multiple full booking-list refetches per successful guest add; a targeted invalidation of the affected list/detail query should be used instead

`&&` instead of `||` in the team permission check (addGuests.handler.ts:46–48): `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` requires the user to be both admin and owner, so team admins who are not owners are incorrectly forbidden
The two sequential awaits for `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` could be parallelized with `Promise.all`

Case-sensitive email comparisons break dedupe and the blacklist: `guest === attendee.email` is exact-case and `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased while guests are not normalized, so `Spam@X.com` bypasses a `spam@x.com` blacklist entry and case-variant duplicates create duplicate attendee rows (duplicate emails/ICS entries); the client-side uniqueness check in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26–29 has the same exact-case flaw — emails should be normalized to lowercase before all comparisons

No transaction or partial-failure handling: attendees are persisted via `prisma.booking.update` before `updateCalendarAttendees`, which is not wrapped in try/catch, so if the calendar update throws the handler errors after the DB write — the UI reports failure while the guests were actually persisted and no emails were sent
In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46-48, the team permission check uses `&&` instead of `||`, contradicting the variable's own name `isTeamAdminOrOwner`

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Exact-string comparison (guest === attendee.email) lets case variants defeat the duplicate guest filter, allowing the same person to be added twice

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the duplicate filter uses a case-sensitive comparison: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`. Since `guest` is taken directly from input (only validated as `.email()`), a user can submit a casing variant (e.g., `User@Example.com` vs `user@example.com`) that will not match an existing attendee email string, allowing the same underlying email address to be added again. The blacklist is lowercased but `guest` is not, reinforcing the lack of normalization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No upper bound on the guests array (no .max()) and no rate limiting on the mutation, so any authorized user (including a mere attendee) can submit thousands of emails in one request, each producing a DB row and a full-details scheduled email — an outbound spam/DoS vector

adjudication.rationale: The new mutation input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` allows `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max()`, and the handler `addGuestsHandler` does `createMany` with `guestsFullDetails` derived from the provided list, so a very large array will create many DB rows in one call. The handler also calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which iterates over attendees and sends emails, amplifying the cost. Authorization explicitly allows `isAttendee` (`booking.attendees.find(...)`) to proceed, meaning a normal attendee can invoke this. No rate limiting or other throttling is shown in the diff. This makes the “thousands of emails in one request” spam/DoS vector a real issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar update uses the requester's credentials instead of the organizer's: getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) is passed to EventManager while the organizer's credentials (explicitly included in the booking query) are never used, so when a non-organizer adds guests, updateCalendarAttendees runs with the wrong or empty credential set and guests are never added to the organizer's actual calendar event (or the update errors out)

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the booking query includes booking.user.credentials (and booking.user.destinationCalendar), implying organizer/account credentials are available. However, the calendar update path uses `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and instantiates `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })`, where `user` is the requester (ctx.user). Since the mutation explicitly allows non-organizers (team admin/owner, or an attendee) to add guests, this means `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will run with the requester's credentials rather than the organizer's. For non-organizers, this can be the wrong credential set (or empty), so the organizer’s calendar event may not be updated correctly. The included organizer credentials are never used, reinforcing that this is an introduced correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Raw guests array is passed to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of uniqueGuests, so an existing attendee whose email appears in the filtered-out list matches newGuests.includes(attendee.email) in email-manager.ts and receives a full AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the correct guests-added notification

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the server filters the input `guests` into `uniqueGuests` (excluding existing attendees and blacklisted emails) and only persists `uniqueGuests`. However it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` using the original unfiltered array. In email-manager.ts, `sendAddGuestsEmails` checks `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` to decide which template to send; if the caller included an email that was already an attendee (thus filtered out and not newly added), that attendee email is still present in `guests`, so they will incorrectly match and receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No booking status or time check: the findFirst has no status filter, so guests can be added to CANCELLED/REJECTED or long-past bookings, generating CONFIRMED ICS invites and calendar updates for events that no longer exist and misleading recipients

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler`, the booking is fetched with `prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } ... })` and there is no subsequent validation of booking state (e.g., cancelled/rejected) or event timing (e.g., `startTime` already in the past). The handler will always: (1) create new attendee records, (2) call `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, and (3) send emails whose ICS payload explicitly sets `status: "CONFIRMED"` in both new email templates. Given the absence of any status/time guard in the diff, this enables adding guests and issuing confirmed calendar updates/emails for bookings that may no longer be active.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Partial-state failure: eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees is not wrapped in error handling, so if it throws the mutation returns an error even though the guests were already added (no rollback), and a retry behaves unexpectedly

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the new `addGuestsHandler`, the DB update that creates new attendees (`prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`) is executed and committed before `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);`. That call is not inside a `try/catch` and there is no transaction/rollback. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the mutation will error out after having already persisted the guests, leaving the system in a partially-updated state (DB updated, calendar not). A retry can then behave unexpectedly because `uniqueGuests` filters out already-added attendees and may become empty, triggering `BAD_REQUEST` (`emails_must_be_unique_valid`). This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email sending errors are swallowed: the catch block logs only a static string (Error sending AddGuestsEmails) and discards err, making delivery failures invisible

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the call to `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is wrapped in a `try/catch` that only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and does not log `err` or rethrow it. This means email delivery failures are effectively swallowed and the underlying error details are discarded, making such failures hard to detect or debug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stale validation error in AddGuestsDialog.tsx: setIsInvalidEmail(true) is never reset when the user retries with corrected input (only cleared via the Cancel button), so the error banner persists after the input becomes valid

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when validation fails in `handleAdd`, but it is never set back to `false` when validation succeeds or when the user edits the input. The only reset is inside the Cancel button handler. As a result, after one invalid attempt, the error banner (`{isInvalidEmail && ...}`) will continue to render even if the user corrects the emails and retries successfully (and it may also remain true across dialog close/reopen since the component stays mounted).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The `guests` array in addGuests.schema.ts has no `.max()` cap, so a single authenticated request can submit thousands of emails, driving unbounded `createMany` rows, unbounded calendar API attendee pushes, and unbounded email fan-out — SMTP/provider quota exhaustion, sender-IP reputation damage (an email-bombing/spam vector through the mail infrastructure), DB bloat, and CPU burn

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.schema.ts`, `guests` is validated only as `z.array(z.string().email())` with no upper bound. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler then (1) derives `uniqueGuests` from that input, (2) does `attendees.createMany` with `data: guestsFullDetails` (one DB row per guest), (3) calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` which will push the full attendee list to the calendar integration, and (4) calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which fans out emails over `calendarEvent.attendees.map(...)`. Because this endpoint is available to any authenticated organizer *or even an existing attendee* (`isAttendee` check), a single permitted request can submit a very large `guests` array and trigger large DB writes + external calendar updates + mass email sending. Nothing in the diff adds rate limiting or size limits, so the unbounded-input/abuse vector described is verifiably present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Every add-guests call re-emails all existing attendees rather than just the new guests, so repeated calls amplify email volume to roughly k×N emails
matched_golden_ids: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying bug: the add-guests email flow iterates over the full existing attendees list (not just the newly added guests), causing already-invited attendees to receive emails again. The golden comment frames it as using calendarEvent.attendees while checking against the input guests list, which results in incorrect targeting/classification; the candidate captures the practical effect (re-emailing all attendees on each call).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Each fanned-out email requires a full `generateIcsString` call that itself iterates all attendees (O(N²) work per call) plus a React SSR render, all dispatched concurrently via one unbounded `Promise.all`; one ICS payload could be shared per role

adjudication.rationale: In `sendAddGuestsEmails` the code builds an `emailsToSend` array containing one send per organizer, per team member, and per attendee, then runs them all via a single `await Promise.all(emailsToSend)`. Each of the new email templates (`packages/emails/templates/*-add-guests-email.ts`) generates an ICS payload by calling `generateIcsString({ event: this.calEvent, ... })` and also renders HTML via `renderEmail(...)` inside `getNodeMailerPayload()`. Because `this.calEvent` includes the full `attendees` list, if `generateIcsString` enumerates attendees (typical for ICS ATTENDEE lines), doing that once per recipient means total work scales with recipients × attendees (quadratic in attendee count when recipients ~ attendees). The diff also shows no concurrency limiting, so a booking with many attendees/team members will dispatch many expensive render+ICS operations concurrently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts fetches the organizer's credentials via `include: { credentials: true }` (heavy OAuth token blobs) but never reads them, while `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` issues a second credentials query for the requester — a duplicate load when the requester is the organizer, and in the attendee-initiated path the EventManager is built from the wrong user's credentials, causing `updateCalendarAttendees` to no-op or error against the organizer's calendar references

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the booking is fetched with `include: { user: { include: { credentials: true }}}`, but that loaded `booking.user.credentials` is never referenced anywhere afterward. Instead, the code later calls `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and constructs `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...] })` where `user` is the requester (ctx.user), not necessarily the booking organizer. Since `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` is intended to update the booking’s calendar attendees, using the requester’s credentials is a concrete correctness risk when a non-organizer (attendee/team admin) triggers the mutation, because the requester may not have access/credentials to modify the organizer’s calendar event. Additionally, when the requester is the organizer, credentials are likely fetched twice (once via the booking include, again via getUsersCredentials), making the included credentials load redundant/heavy.

adjudication_records.issue_text: N+1 translation loads: `getTranslation(attendee.locale)` is invoked per attendee inside a map, performing O(attendees) i18n resource loads/instantiations on every add-guests request; translations should be cached per distinct locale

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code builds `attendeesListPromises` by mapping over `bookingAttendees.attendees` and, for each attendee, awaits `getTranslation(attendee.locale ?? "en", "common")`. This results in one translation-load/instantiation call per attendee (O(n)) within a single request, even when multiple attendees share the same locale. Since the handler already separately loads `tOrganizer` once, this per-attendee translation loading is redundant and is a classic N+1-style performance issue that could be avoided by caching translations per distinct locale.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Linear-scan membership checks inside loops: `booking.attendees.some(...)` per guest (addGuests.handler.ts:74–78) and `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` per attendee (email-manager.ts:~541) are both O(N×M); a `Set` should be used for lookups

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering `guests` and for each guest it calls `booking.attendees.some(...)`, which scans the attendees array each time (nested iteration). In `email-manager.ts` `sendAddGuestsEmails`, it maps over `calendarEvent.attendees` and for each attendee calls `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`, which linearly scans `newGuests` each time. Both are verifiable O(N×M) membership patterns that could be reduced to O(N+M) by precomputing a `Set` of attendee emails / new guest emails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blanket cache invalidation: `utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate()` in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:37 invalidates every query under `viewer.bookings`, triggering multiple full booking-list refetches per successful guest add; a targeted invalidation of the affected list/detail query should be used instead

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, the `onSuccess` handler calls `utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate()`, which does invalidate all cached queries under the `viewer.bookings` namespace. However, the finding’s claimed impact (“triggering multiple full booking-list refetches per successful guest add” and that this is a problem) is not verifiable from the diff: we cannot see what queries exist, how many are active, or whether this causes problematic refetch behavior in practice. This is more of a performance/optimization suggestion than a clear defect introduced by the change, and blanket invalidation is a common, acceptable correctness-preserving approach to ensure UI consistency after a mutation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `&&` instead of `||` in the team permission check (addGuests.handler.ts:46–48): `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` requires the user to be both admin and owner, so team admins who are not owners are incorrectly forbidden
matched_golden_ids: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue flags the same bug: the permission logic incorrectly uses &&, requiring both admin and owner, and should use || to allow either role. It notes admins who aren’t owners are wrongly forbidden, matching the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The two sequential awaits for `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` could be parallelized with `Promise.all`

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which *does* await sequentially, but this is not a clear defect. The `&&` also intentionally short-circuits: if `isTeamAdmin` is false, `isTeamOwner` is never called. Replacing with `Promise.all` would always invoke both queries and could increase load/change side effects. This is at most a micro-optimization suggestion, not a verifiable bug/security/correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Case-sensitive email comparisons break dedupe and the blacklist: `guest === attendee.email` is exact-case and `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased while guests are not normalized, so `Spam@X.com` bypasses a `spam@x.com` blacklist entry and case-variant duplicates create duplicate attendee rows (duplicate emails/ICS entries); the client-side uniqueness check in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26–29 has the same exact-case flaw — emails should be normalized to lowercase before all comparisons

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In addGuests.handler.ts, guests are compared case-sensitively: duplicates are filtered with `guest === attendee.email`, so `Spam@x.com` and `spam@x.com` are treated as different and can both be inserted via `createMany`, creating duplicate attendee rows/notifications. The blacklist is lowercased (`BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.split(...).map(toLowerCase())`) but checked with `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`, so a case-variant guest email can bypass the blacklist. On the client, AddGuestsDialog.tsx builds a uniqueness Set over raw strings, so it also fails to catch case-variant duplicates before submitting. All of these behaviors are directly present in the diff and are correctness/security-relevant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No transaction or partial-failure handling: attendees are persisted via `prisma.booking.update` before `updateCalendarAttendees`, which is not wrapped in try/catch, so if the calendar update throws the handler errors after the DB write — the UI reports failure while the guests were actually persisted and no emails were sent

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler first persists new attendees via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and only afterward calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);`. That calendar update is not wrapped in a `try/catch` and there is no transaction spanning the DB write + calendar update + email sending. Therefore, if `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the mutation will error back to the client after the DB write has already succeeded; the UI will go through the `onError` path while the guests were actually added in the database and the subsequent email sending will not execute.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46-48, the team permission check uses `&&` instead of `||`, contradicting the variable's own name `isTeamAdminOrOwner`

adjudication.rationale:
The diff introduces this authorization logic:

```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
  (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
  (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```

Despite the variable name `isTeamAdminOrOwner`, it requires the user to be **both** a team admin **and** a team owner. This will deny access to users who are only admins (or only owners), making the permission check stricter than the name (and typical intent) indicates. The redundancy of checking both roles also suggests this is unintended and should likely be `||`.

Because this directly affects the `FORBIDDEN` decision, it’s a real correctness/authorization bug in the diff.
